analysis:
Only .github/workflows/release-swift.yml changed, in two ways.

(1) The build-provider job now sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT from needs.resolve-env.outputs.environment (head hunk at ~line 131). The value comes from a workflow_dispatch choice (dev|prod) or a tag-derived value in scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh. It is not attacker-controlled free text. The qualify-sdk job deliberately does not set it, so tests run against production defaults. The qualification lane therefore compiles different defaults than the shipped dev artifact. That is not a regression, because durable App Attest build qualification (A-017, T-054) approves the exact signed binary and full CodeDirectory, not the qualify-sdk output.

(2) Two new fail-closed greps require 'build-environment-runtime-smoke: <ENV_PREFIX> ' in the runtime-smoke output. One runs pre-sign (base ~line 480) and one on the final extracted signed artifact (base ~line 758). ENV_PREFIX is defined at build-and-release job env (base line 206). This checks the unsigned build's baked environment against the signing job's environment, including on the resume path. It reduces the risk of a dev-compiled binary being signed and published as prod, or the reverse. This relates to T-054, TB-011 and the release admission and publication boundary. The marker is self-reported by the binary, but the binary is the artifact whose hashes are later registered, so it is a consistency check rather than a trust root.

No secrets are exposed, no new permissions are added, and the release-key and qualification separation is unchanged.

Coverage limit: the Package.swift environment-default compilation and the Swift runtime-smoke emitter for build-environment-runtime-smoke were not in the supplied units. Their correctness (for example, that defaults such as the coordinator URL really differ per environment, and that the marker cannot be spoofed by a stale default) is unverified here. A later pass should check those files if they are in the PR.
